records.name: Resurrection of Our Lord Parish
records.summary: The young adult ministry of a Catholic parish at Castor Avenue and Vista Street, for people aged 18 to 35. Its groups meet for Bible study, social mixers, talks and retreats, and the parish holds four Sunday Masses plus a weekday morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Join a young adult group for Bible study, Theology on Tap at local bars, socials and dances, speakers, retreats or pilgrimages, and come to Mass. The page gives no meeting times, so ask the parish office which group meets when. The parish also lists a Portuguese Apostolate, faith formation, RCIA, and ministry to the sick and homebound.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 6:30, 8:30 and 10:30 am and at noon. Weekday Mass at 8:30 am. Saturday confession 3:30 to 4:15 pm, Sunday confession at 10 am, or by appointment.

first_step.how: Come to any listed Mass, then email or call the parish office to ask which young adult group meets next.
first_step.basis: The pastor's I'm New page invites newcomers to visit and contact the parish office, though the young adult page gives no sign-up or meeting times.
first_step.what_to_expect: The young adult ministry runs groups with weekly, monthly and yearly gatherings, such as Bible study, socials, dances, talks, retreats and pilgrimages. Mass is free, and a first visit can be as simple as attending a Sunday Mass and asking the office about the next gathering. The website does not list meeting days or times for the groups, so the office is the best source.
first_visit_tips: Call or email the parish office before you come, since the young adult pages give no meeting times.
The parish's I'm New page is the place to start for newcomers.
Parking and transit are not listed on the parish pages, so ask when you call.

records.notes: Young adult meeting days and times are not on the young adult page, the I'm New page, or the parish bulletin web page. The bulletin's latest listed edition is dated October 11, 2026, its PDF did not load, and its web page text had no young adult items. The Facebook page of the local young adult group is this record's own social link and was not read, since Facebook is lead only. Crowd changed from all_ages to young_adults to match the 18 to 35 range. Mass details are carried from tier 1. The archdiocesan young adult site named on the parish page did not resolve, so it is listed under blocked.

records.name: Rev UP Philly
records.summary: A monthly open meeting for people working to make Philadelphia better for people with disabilities and seniors. Residents, workers and organizations come together online to plan change.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly video meeting, share ideas, and sign up to help with disability and senior issues across the city.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on a Wednesday from 3 to 4:30 pm, held on Zoom

access.notes: The meeting page says nothing about captions or ASL. The host organization's accessibility statement says its virtual events include live captions or transcripts, with ASL on request, and asks for accommodation requests seven days ahead at Access@DisabilityPridePA.org.

first_step.how: Fill in the short sign-up form linked from the event page, then join the next monthly Zoom meeting.
first_step.basis: The meeting is open to anyone interested in disability and senior issues in Philadelphia and links a sign-up form, but it does not say newcomers are specifically welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The meeting is a video call on Zoom that runs about an hour and a half on a Wednesday afternoon. Residents, workers and organizations share ideas for changes that matter to people with disabilities and seniors in the city. The page does not describe the agenda in detail and mentions no fees or dues.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the sign-up form on the event page before the meeting.
You need a computer, tablet or phone with internet access to join the Zoom call.
Ask for any accommodation at least seven days ahead by emailing Access@DisabilityPridePA.org.

records.notes: The event page's latest dated meeting is February 18, 2026, and no later meeting appears in the copy read, so the last sign of life rests on that date. The join link on the Rev UP page leads to a short sign-up form, which is not recorded here. The Board Member Application on the same site belongs to Disability Pride Pennsylvania and was left out. The event page's Zoom meeting ID and passcode were not recorded.

records.name: Revolution Shakespeare
records.summary: A Philadelphia company that puts on Shakespeare in new forms, including adaptations, readings and digital work, with a focus on how audiences hear and learn from the plays.
records.what_you_do: Watch its productions, which have included free outdoor shows in city parks, or follow its readings and digital programs. To ask about auditions or helping out, email the company, since its site lists no open calls.

locations.label: Mailing address, c/o The Painted Bride Arts Center, Project Space

first_step.how: Email revolutionshakespeare@gmail.com to ask about audition calls or helping out. The newsletter signup also sends audition news, but its form showed a setup note when checked, so email is the surer route.
first_step.basis: The site names no open audition, class or volunteer role, and the only ways in are an email address and a newsletter form that may not be working, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The company's site lists no open classes, rehearsals or volunteer shifts, so a first step is an email. Its 2026 Hamlet ran as free outdoor shows in parks in late July and early August, with shows starting around 7 pm, and the site lists no future dates. Ask the company about dates and seating before you come.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the site has no event calendar.
The mailing address is c/o The Painted Bride Arts Center, so it is not a place to visit in person.

records.notes: The homepage gives the mailing address as c/o The Painted Bride Arts Center, Project Space, 4029 Cambridge Street, which matches tier 1. The newsletter signup says it sends occasional audition, production and performance news, and the form shows a setup note, so it may not be working. The contact page lists no phone and no visit policy. The Digital Programming and Past Productions pages were not read. The 2021 ASAP Drama club programs are in leads_only.

records.name: Rhawnhurst Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on Loretto Avenue with an 11 am Sunday service, a 10 am coffee hour, and outreach and mission ministries.
records.what_you_do: Come to the 11 am service, join the coffee hour, or ask about outreach and mission work through the contact page.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, with a coffee hour at 10 am

first_step.how: Come to the 11 am Sunday service at 7701 Loretto Avenue, or email the church first to talk with a pastor or elder before your visit.
first_step.basis: The church says visitors can talk with a pastor or elder through its contact page, greeters welcome people, and the homepage invites visitors to Sunday worship, though no newcomer class is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship is at 11 am in the main sanctuary, with hymn singing, prayer, and Bible-centered preaching from rotating guest pastors. The site does not say how long the service runs. Children from infancy through age 5 can go to nursery, and children ages 5 through fifth grade attend junior church during the service.
first_visit_tips: Come as you are; the about page says dress is not a concern.
The site gives no parking or entrance details, so email rpc19111@gmail.com or call 215-342-2112 before a first visit.
Ask a greeter about nursery or junior church for children.

records.notes: The homepage lists 2026 Communion Sundays (January 4, February 22, April 2, May 24, October 4 and November 22). October 4, 2026 is the newest past date with a year, so it sets last_sign_of_life. This is a published schedule, not a dated news post, so confidence stays at medium. The calendar page shows a member login and no public events. No accessibility details (parking, ramp, hearing assist) are published, so access is left out. Outreach and Missions are named as ministries without descriptions.

records.name: Rittenhop
records.summary: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday afternoon in Rittenhouse Square, with jam sessions, jazz events and a holiday party.
records.what_you_do: Come dance the Sunday swing, or bring a horn to a jam session. The group also runs jazz events and a jazz crawl.

schedule.text: Sundays, 1 to 3:30 pm, rain or shine. Jam sessions and special dates are posted on the site, and weather or venue changes go out on Discord.

locations.label: Rittenhouse Square (usually the southwest corner, by the bench with the goat statue)

cost.text: Free. Donations help cover tech costs and pay for live bands.

first_step.how: Go to Rittenhouse Square on a Sunday between 1 and 3:30 pm, look for the bench with the goat statue in the southwest corner, and join in.
first_step.basis: Free and open to anyone who shows up, and the about page sets no experience requirement, but formal lessons at the dance are rare, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a free, DJ'd swing dance on the square's brick surface, mostly Lindy Hop and Charleston, with all jazz dance styles welcome. Formal lessons are rare at the Sunday dance, though some regulars may show newcomers a few basics. The dance runs rain or shine, and it is sometimes held in the center of the park instead of the southwest corner.
first_visit_tips: Check the website and Discord around 1 pm on the day, since weather or venue changes are posted there.
Wear shoes you can dance in, since the square's surface is brick.
For a lesson first, the about page points to a Thursday beginner class across the street run by Jazz Attack. Check its time and price with them, since listings differ.

records.notes: Conflict on the dance start time: the homepage says 1 to 3:30 pm and the events page says 1:30 to 3:30 pm. The record keeps 1 to 3:30 pm from the homepage, so confirm on site. The about page names a Thursday beginner lesson run by Jazz Attack across the street, at 8 pm for $10 per that page. A separate search result gave a $7 drop-in and a different venue, so the record gives only the pointer, not the time or price. Jazz Crawl 2027 is listed for the first or second Saturday of April 2027, with no details yet. The group mentions a Discord server, but no link was found on the pages read, so none is recorded.

records.name: Rittenhouse Astronomical Society
records.summary: An astronomy society founded in 1888 that runs public talks with guest speakers and keeps the public posted through a mailing list.
records.what_you_do: Come to a public open house at Ryan Observatory, usually on the second Saturday evening, or to one of the city nights at Columbus Recreation Center. Members get dark-sky observing, virtual access to the monthly meetings, and a free seat at the telescope workshop.

schedule.text: Public open houses at Ryan Observatory fall on the second Saturday of most months, starting at 7:15 pm. Observing nights at the observatory are scheduled around sunset, weather permitting.

locations.label: Ryan Observatory, Muddy Run Park, Holtwood, PA
Columbus Recreation Center, 8th and Wharton, Philadelphia

cost.text: Open house prices are not listed. Yearly membership is $50 (Star), $75 (Supernova) or $350 (Quasar). Members get the telescope workshop free, and non-members buy a ticket.

first_step.how: Come to a public open house at Ryan Observatory on a second Saturday evening. The next one is Saturday, October 10, 2026, starting at 7:15 pm. No registration is listed for open houses, and the contact page offers a mailing list for updates.
first_step.basis: Open houses are public with no registration listed, the society says no experience is needed to attend, and it runs telescope workshops that non-members buy a ticket to.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open houses run from 7:15 pm to about 10 pm, usually with a talk or themed program at the observatory. Observing nights depend on the weather, so check the events page before you go. The observatory is in Muddy Run Park in Holtwood, outside the city, so plan your ride ahead.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page the week before, since observing nights depend on the weather.
Plan transport to Holtwood, since the observatory is outside the city.
The telescope workshop is free for members and needs a ticket for non-members, so ask about it if you want hands-on learning.

records.notes: The events page lists Ryan Observatory open houses on October 10, November 14 and December 12, 2026, all starting at 7:15 pm. The events page gives no city for Ryan Observatory or Columbus Recreation Center, so the Holtwood location is from the tier 1 read of the homepage. The society's mailing office is in Media, PA (Delaware County), which is not a visit place. The events page has internal time conflicts (for example the May 9, 2026 open house), so only the 7:15 pm start is given. The membership page does not mention workshops, so workshop details come from the events page. Members-only Zoom gatherings and member or volunteer observing nights are not recorded as public events.

records.name: RiverWays Collaboration
records.summary: A partnership that gets more people onto the water in Philadelphia and nearby, especially in communities that have had little access. Its Thursday sunset paddles at Cherry Street Pier in October cost only a $10 seat donation, refunded on arrival, and it lists youth camps and boat building run by partner groups.
records.what_you_do: Register for a Thursday sunset paddle (ages 12 and up), sign a young person up for a camp or boat build with a partner group, or check the water access map.

schedule.text: Free Sunset Paddles on Thursday evenings in October at Cherry St Pier, 4:30 to 7 pm, with registration. Camps and after-school programs are listed separately.

cost.text: Paddles are free to join, with a $10 seat donation refunded when you arrive. Other program costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Register for a Thursday sunset paddle through the Zeffy link on the events calendar, paying the $10 seat donation, which is refunded when you arrive.
first_step.basis: The page says no paddling or swim experience is needed, equipment and instruction are provided, and it links a registration form, so the way in is clear for beginners.
first_step.what_to_expect: Paddles are single-seat kayaks, about 2 to 3 miles round trip on the Delaware River, from 4:30 to 7 pm on Thursdays in October. Equipment and instruction are provided, and no paddling or swim experience is needed. Paddlers must be 12 or older.
first_visit_tips: Pay the $10 seat donation when you register; it is refunded when you arrive.
Paddlers must be 12 or older.
If you bring your own boat, you still need to register.

records.notes: The paddle listing says Thursdays in October without a year, so the season is set to fall. The calendar lists The Big Paddle 2026 on September 12, 2026, and the event page marks a 2027 edition as tentative for September 18, 2027, with a rain date of September 19. Boat building programs (UrbanPromise Boatworks in Camden, NJ, and Glen Foerd's Waterborne at partner schools) are for middle and high school students. Camps are run by partner groups, and their dates and prices are not stated on Riverways' page, so none are recorded. Free Fishing with Friends at Pier 68 and Glen Foerd family fishing nights are on the calendar but are not in this record. The Youth Council fall cohort is undated. Adventure Aquarium in Camden, NJ, is named on the camps page and is not a Philadelphia group.

notes: Seven records, all publish, all tier 2. One WebSearch used of one allowed (Jazz Attack lookup); its results conflicted, so the record states only what Rittenhop's own page says about that lesson. 28 WebFetch calls used of 60, including two failed DNS attempts and one redirect followed. Tier 1 fields were carried over unless a page showed otherwise. Corrections: Resurrection crowd changed to young_adults and summary narrowed to the young adult ministry; Riverways summary and first step corrected (paddles need a refundable $10 seat donation and registration; camps are run by partner groups); Rittenhouse Astronomical Society what_you_do corrected (members get dark-sky observing, virtual meetings and a telescope workshop seat); Rhawnhurst status moved to active on the 2026 Communion Sunday dates listed on its homepage, a published schedule rather than a dated news post. Rittenhouse Astronomical Society's office is in Media, PA, which is not a visit place.
